Buying gold jewellery in Nepal is a major purchase, so checking purity before you pay is essential. The rate you see as the gold price in nepal today applies to hallmark (fine) gold — if the jewellery you are buying is not actually that pure, you are overpaying. This guide explains every practical way to verify gold purity in Nepal, from the hallmark stamp to laboratory testing.

First, Understand Carat: 24K, 22K and 18K

Purity is measured in carats (K). 24 carat gold is 99.9% pure — in Nepal this is called chhapawal (hallmark) gold, and it is the quality the daily FENEGOSIDA rate refers to. Jewellery is usually made softer by mixing alloys:

  • 24K (99.9%) — fine/hallmark gold, used for coins, bars and the benchmark rate.
  • 22K (91.6%) — common for jewellery; durable enough for daily wear.
  • 18K (75%) — harder, often used for diamond and stone settings.

When a shop quotes you the day's rate, always ask: is this price for 24K hallmark or for a lower carat? A lower-carat piece should cost proportionally less than the hallmark rate. You can compare with our gold rate calculator before visiting the shop.

Method 1: Check the Hallmark Stamp

The fastest check is the hallmark itself. Hallmark-certified gold in Nepal is tested and stamped by an authorised assay centre under the Nepal Bureau of Standards and Metrology (NBSM) system. Look on the inside of a ring, the clasp of a necklace, or the back of an earring for tiny engraved marks:

  • The purity number — e.g. 999 for 24K, 916 for 22K.
  • The hallmark logo of the certifying assay centre.
  • The jeweller's own mark.

If a piece has no stamp at all, treat that as a warning sign and ask the seller to get it assayed before you buy.

Method 2: The Touchstone (Kasauti) Test

Jewellers traditionally rub the gold on a black touchstone (kasauti) and apply nitric acid drops. The colour and survival of the streak indicate purity: pure gold resists the acid, while lower-carat streaks fade. This test is quick and free at most established shops, but it only tests the surface — a gold-plated piece can pass it. Use it as a first screen, not final proof.

Method 3: XRF Machine Testing (Most Reliable)

An XRF (X-ray fluorescence) analyser reads the exact metal composition in seconds without damaging the piece. Many assay offices and larger jewellery showrooms in Kathmandu and other cities have XRF machines, and testing usually costs a few hundred rupees. For any purchase above a few tola, an XRF report is worth it — it catches plated and filled items that the touchstone misses. Ask for the printed reading and match the percentage against the carat you are paying for.

Method 4: Density, Magnet and Home Checks

  • Magnet test: real gold is not magnetic. If a piece is strongly attracted to a magnet, it is not solid gold. (Clasps may contain steel springs, so test the main body.)
  • Weight and size: gold is dense — a genuine piece feels heavier than an imitation of the same size.
  • Skin and smell tests are myths: they cannot confirm purity. Rely on the stamp, the touchstone and XRF instead.

Buying Safely in Nepal: A Short Checklist

  • Check the day's rate first — see the gold price in nepal today and the gold price history so you know the fair range.
  • Buy only hallmark-stamped jewellery and insist on a proper bill showing weight, purity, making charge and the day's rate separately.
  • Ask about the buy-back policy in writing — how much is deducted when you sell or exchange.
  • For old or inherited gold, get an XRF test before accepting any exchange valuation.
  • Remember the daily rate already includes the standard charges set by the federation; compare making charges between 2–3 shops.

What About Silver?

The same discipline applies to silver. Check today's silver price in Nepal before buying, and look for the 999 or 925 (sterling) stamp on silver jewellery and utensils.

Once you know how to verify purity, it also helps to understand where prices are heading — read our analysis of current trends in the Nepal gold market. And before any big purchase, always re-check the live gold price in nepal today — rates change every working day.

Gold in Nepal has had an extraordinary run. From around NPR 277,300 per tola in early July 2026, the price climbed to a record NPR 322,700 per tola on August 24, 2026 — then corrected sharply, opening after the Dashain break at NPR 278,500 per tola on October 25. This analysis breaks down what actually moved the market, using the daily FENEGOSIDA rates recorded on this site.

The 2026 Story So Far

Three phases stand out in this year's gold price history:

  • April–May: high plateau. Gold traded mostly between NPR 290,000 and NPR 302,800 per tola, already expensive by historical standards, with silver peaking near NPR 5,345 per tola.
  • May 31: the budget shock. The government's budget raised the customs duty on gold from 10% to 20%. The rate jumped in a single step from NPR 290,600 (May 29) to NPR 311,100 per tola — one of the largest policy-driven moves on record.
  • August peak, autumn correction. International strength pushed gold to its all-time high of NPR 322,700 on August 24. Profit-taking abroad and a softer dollar then pulled it down through September (NPR 288,400–299,300), and after the Dashain market closure it reopened at NPR 278,500 — down NPR 11,700 from the pre-holiday rate of NPR 290,200.

What Actually Drives Nepal's Gold Price?

1. The international bullion market

Nepal imports all of its gold, so the London/global spot price is the base. When global gold rises, the FENEGOSIDA rate follows within a day — you can watch this pass-through on the gold price in nepal today page.

2. The USD–NPR exchange rate

Gold is bought in dollars. A weaker Nepali rupee makes every tola more expensive even if the world price does not move. Because the NPR is pegged to the Indian rupee, India's currency moves matter too.

3. Government duty and taxes

As May 31 proved, policy can move the price more in one day than the market does in a month. The customs duty hike to 20% (plus luxury tax considerations on jewellery) permanently lifted the local premium over the international price.

4. Seasonal demand

Demand peaks around Dashain and Tihar and during the wedding seasons (Mangsir and Magh–Falgun). Smuggling and unofficial imports also expand whenever the official price gap with India grows, which can distort local availability.

5. Import quota

Nepal Rastra Bank limits how much gold banks can import daily. When demand exceeds the quota in festival season, shops may run short of stock even while the official rate is unchanged.

Silver: The Quieter, Wilder Ride

Silver followed gold up — reaching about NPR 5,345 per tola in late May — and fell harder, dropping to NPR 3,955 per tola by October 25. Silver's smaller, more industrial market makes it more volatile in both directions. Track it alongside gold on our silver price in Nepal page.

What Should Buyers and Investors Watch Next?

  • Global direction: if international gold resumes its climb, Nepal's rate will follow quickly; corrections abroad pass through just as fast, as October showed.
  • Festival demand: Tihar and the wedding season typically firm up prices and premiums — buying a little before peak season has historically helped, though past patterns never guarantee the future.
  • Policy: any change to the 20% customs duty or the import quota would move the local price immediately.
  • Purity before price: whatever the trend, never pay the 24K rate for untested metal — follow our guide on how to check gold purity in Nepal.

Bottom line: 2026 has rewarded patience — the post-Dashain dip to NPR 278,500 is roughly 14% below the August record. Whether that is a buying opportunity depends on the global market, but the smart approach is unchanged: follow the daily gold price in nepal today, buy hallmark gold from a transparent seller, and use the gold rate calculator to check the full cost including making charges before you commit.
